test.name: Spec 0010 spike: process group members with proc_listpids

expected: proc_listpids(PROC_PGRP_ONLY, group) lists every process in a group, also after the group leader exited and was reaped (spec 0010 AC-5, Adapter macOS row Anggota group)
actual: A /bin/sh leader with two /bin/sleep children (own group via SETSID): proc_listpids(PROC_PGRP_ONLY) returns the 3 pids. After `sleep 30 & exit 0` exited and was reaped, the leftover sleep (now ppid 1) is still listed under the old leader's pgid; after kill(-pgid, SIGKILL) the list is empty. libproc's proc_listpgrppids returns a count of pids, not bytes (3), unlike proc_listpids, which returns bytes. libc 0.2.190 has no PROC_PGRP_ONLY (2), so the adapter declares it.
steps: Checked out d99e5ea (clean) in worktree f10-spike-a90e60 on this Mac (macOS 27.0 build 26A428, arm64, Apple Silicon, page size 16384).
cargo build -p stackly-fake-server --locked; the child in every scenario is target/debug/stackly-fake-server (or /bin/sh and /bin/sleep where a process group or a descendant is needed).

Built the throwaway spike outside the workspace: spike-main.rs.txt as src/main.rs and spike-Cargo.toml.txt as Cargo.toml (libc =0.2.190, the workspace's version, plus serde_json), cargo build --offline --release. Source, full run log, and the extra experiments are in the evidence folder of the first record of this set (title 'Spec 0010 spike: posix_spawn flags, fd map, argv, env, cwd').
